title: Texas Roadhouse talks ribs for Father's Day
description: The restaurant's famous, fall-off-the-bone ribs are being celebrated this weekend.  Plus, catch your chance to win a free barbecue grill.

asr.full_text: It's perfect grilling weather so we're really taking advantage of that this morning with Texas Roadhouse. You know, Father's Day is around the corner. That's one of the reasons why we're out here is because, you know, Father's Day is coming. Men like to eat, you know, all types of different meat. It's summertime. And, of course, Texas Roadhouse is kind enough to be cooking up some of their famous ribs. So, of course, we're going to be out here to join them. And, in fact, with us this morning is Zach Knoll from Texas Roadhouse. Great. Thanks so much for being with us. You guys are cooking up a ton of ribs out here this morning and it looks like you've. Kind of split up the jobs with Fisher back there. He's manning the grill. So tell us a little bit about what you guys do to prepare these delicious looking ribs. First of all, it's the quality of the product. We don't use anything other than American grown pork, baby, or not baby, but pork back. Loin ribs that we bring in fresh and then it's all about time and patience. How long do these take to prep? It's a three day process. Oh wow. So, you know, we have not only top quality meat, but we have top quality ingredients. That we do also have on our website for our seasoning. But we season them, we pan them, we let them marinate, we cook them over a long period. Of time, then we cool them down, and then bring them onto our grill and baste them like. You see Fisher here doing with our barbecue sauce. So I imagine in the kitchen at Texas Roadhouse you guys probably have, I mean racks upon. Rack, dozens and dozens of racks at any given time in various stages of the process, right? Yes, you know we have them through a really tight rotation so that the freshest possible. Product, the ribs that come out of the oven this morning is what we're serving on that. Shift and then the same thing for the next day so it's as fresh as you can possibly get. Every single day you come to our restaurant. And freshness is what we like and if we can get a little bit of a shot back here as well,. Again this is Fisher who's manning the grill here, can you tell us a little bit about the. Sauce that you're using? This is just our standard Roadhouse sauce that we use for our ribs here at Texas Roadhouse. As well as some other stuff, barbecue chicken and whatnot. We're just using it to bring out the flavor here. Generous. As you can see, we put a lot on there. And it never really hurts to do a lot of barbecue sauce when you're manning the grill, right? I don't think so. I mean, from a kitchen manager standpoint, I think the quality is a lot better when you've got nice, juicy, saucy ribs. Okay, and quickly, I know that there's been an E. coli scare around the country, especially. Some health experts are a little worried as people start firing up their grills. Tell us quickly some of the things that people need to know when they're dealing with pork. If they're doing pork at all at home, what kind of temperatures, what kind of time, that. Sort of thing? Basically, you just want to make sure that you're taking the time. Minimum safe reheat temperature on pork, for instance, any food, be 165 internal temperature. And that's something that we're at Roadhouse, we're very passionate about is temping out. Every single piece of meat that comes out of our kitchen. And especially with pork, you want to make sure that you don't have any salmonella,. E. coli, any of those issues, and we know you guys are doing it right then. So a lot of good stuff on the grill, of course. Some steaks over here as well, Texas Roadhouse known for their hand-cut steaks as well. And as you, ooh, what do you have going on here, Zach? I got a little liquid smoke and some water. Liquid smoke and water. And so these are going to need to be in there for a while too, now that you've finally. Gotten the liquid going. Well, what we're going to do is Luis is going to bring me some plastic wrap and some aluminum. Foil and we're going to wrap these up and get them ready to go into the oven. And then I'll show you kind of what it looks like when it comes out because if you take. These out of the oven right away... That is massive amounts of foil right there. I need something that big at home. If you take these out of the oven right away and then put them on the grill, what's going. To happen is that those ribs are going to fall right apart. And they're going to be impossible to... Salvage from the flames beneath. Exactly. So the idea is that you want to cool these down. All the way down below 40 degrees as quickly as possible. He's going to show me and show everybody. At home what that looks like. Okay. And then we're going to show you kind of how the best way to. Prepare to get them ready for the grill. So these right here have already been taken down to 40. Degrees. Yep. Took these out of the oven this morning. And then these are going to be, this is. This is what you want to do before you get them on the grill so they're not falling apart. And all that kind of stuff. Yep. So what you're going to do is you're just going to take your knife here, cut between. The bones. You have those two like that. I was going to say, you guys cook, I mean, it's easiest to cook them in bigger pieces,. Right? So quickly, just to wrap up, we've got some big Father's Day stuff coming up at Texas. Roadhouse as well. Correct. Just quickly tell us about that. Yeah, we do have our Father's Day celebration going on this weekend as well as our Rib Fest. Every year in June we celebrate our legendary call up the bone ribs. We're also giving away a nice smoker slash grill in the restaurant so you come on in,. You order some ribs, enter to win that grill and we're just celebrating how we do ribs. All year. Celebrating food. I love that kind of celebration. Thanks so much.
